_comment: ADR-0562 intelligence capability move, SUB-BATCH (c): the supervisor seat-pooling vertical, MINUS its facade. The batch boundary is a DEPENDENCY BOUNDARY, not a count. The closed component of the oya/intelligence graph is NINE crates (these eight plus oya-intelligence-supervisor-app); supervisor-app is DELIBERATELY HELD BACK and the reason is recorded below, so the eight moved here are exactly the component's non-facade members. Verified mechanically in both directions: (out) every path-dep of every crate here resolves either inside this batch or into an ALREADY-LANDED intelligence/core/* or libs/* crate, so nothing points at a crate that has not moved; (in) the only Cargo.toml/BUCK referrers of these eight outside their own dirs are other crates in the component, and the one referrer left behind (supervisor-app, still in oya/intelligence/crates) has its path-deps and BUCK labels rewritten by the codemod to the new locations — a cross-root edge identical in shape to the ones sub-batches (a) and (b) already left behind. The remaining 77 oya/intelligence crates are untouched and reference none of these. Preceded in this PR by the REFACTOR half: oya-intelligence-{claude,codex,gemini}-account-adapter were three crates differing only in five values and were collapsed into one BEFORE the move, so the new capability root never receives the triplication (ADR-0562 quadrichotomy: a relocation preserving a monolith's internal shape is a failed reorg). FACES ARE ON DEPENDENCY EVIDENCE, not on crate names (§10.26). ZERO of the eight declares a single `pub trait`, so NONE is a ports/ seam and no ports/ face is created here. core (3): autonomy-ceiling-domain, route-policy-kernel and autonomy-ceiling-app are pure — zero std::fs / std::net / process / reqwest, no [[bin]], and no edge to any adapters/ crate. autonomy-ceiling-app keeps its legacy `-app` tail while landing in core/ because it has NO main.rs and NO [[bin]] and is a pure use-case library over two kernels; this mirrors the landed os/ precedent verbatim (os-move-plan.json put init-app in os/core because face follows evidence while the de-brand keeps the tail). adapters (5): cli-session-driver spawns a vendor subprocess; jsonl-supervisor-adapter and settings-template-adapter do std::fs (settings-template also libc); supervisor-security-adapter and account-adapter-inmemory have no I/O but IMPLEMENT AutonomyCeilingPort and SecretStorePort respectively — ports owned by OTHER crates — which is what makes a crate an adapter rather than a kernel. Every one of the five depends only on core/, so the batch adds no adapters->adapters and no core->adapters edge. DELIBERATELY DEFERRED — oya-intelligence-supervisor-app: it is the component's composition root (the only crate with a [[bin]], and it constructs all five adapters), so facade/ is its only correct face — core/ would invert the layers by making a core crate depend on five adapters. But `intelligence` has NO ports/ face, so ADR-0562's central layering rule makes any new intelligence facade package emit ci/facade/facade-core-layering `facade_core_no_ports_layer`, whose frozen_baseline holds only intelligence-app and intelligence-worker; landing supervisor-app in intelligence/facade/ would therefore be a NEW baseline-block-on-new finding (its BUCK carries 15 //intelligence/core/ labels). Homing it needs an intelligence ports/ layer, or an ADR-0562 §10.6 ruling — a design task, not a move — so it stays in oya/intelligence/crates until that lands. De-brand per ADR-0532/0533: strip the `oya-` prefix and keep the tail (oya-intelligence-X -> intelligence-X), matching the landed sibling shape in intelligence/adapters (authz-cedar-adapter, eventsink-clickhouse-adapter, openbao-adapter). Workspace membership is preserved BY CONSTRUCTION and not by an edit: the source root matches the legacy glob `oya/*/crates/oya-*` and every destination matches one of the shape globs `*/core/*` and `*/adapters/*`, so the resolved member count is unchanged by the move itself. specs/capability-registry.json already lists `oya/intelligence` in the intelligence capability's absorbs_current_dirs, so no registry edit is required. `intelligence/**` is NOT one of the fifteen catalog_liveness.workspace_member_globs roots, so no crate here is under the forward (member-needs-a-row) contract — but all eight carry a registry/catalog row today, and a row whose crate_id no longer resolves is the REVERSE-direction RED, so every row is renamed in artifacts[] alongside its crate. No OWNERS file and no per-service slos/*.openslo.yaml exists for any crate in this batch (oya/intelligence/slos/ is capability-level and moves when the directory is finally vacated; providers-pool-seat-availability.openslo.yaml belongs to provider-pool-app, which is NOT in this batch), so there is nothing to co-move.
